selected_evidence.requirement: /tmp and /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev (program execution, setuid bits, device nodes ignored)
selected_evidence.summary: Live mount output showed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel for both /dev/shm and /tmp immediately after configuration, confirmed again via findmnt

Captured pre-reboot baseline (boot_id 984a7d52...) with both mounts hardened, issued systemctl reboot, polled until node1 responded with new boot_id c9102ed6..., then re-ran findmnt showing /tmp and /dev/shm still mounted with nosuid,nodev,noexec after the restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof that execution/setuid is actually blocked, not just flagged
selected_evidence.summary: Post-reboot, attempting to execute a script placed in /tmp and a binary copied into /dev/shm both failed with 'Permission denied' and exit code 126

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (boot identity + service/data health before and after restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Boot_id captured before (984a7d52-3387-4830-a06e-15e8b5e6c2a1) and after (c9102ed6-bd24-46f2-bfa3-bab32ddf3bc6) reboot differ, proving a genuine restart; connection timeouts/reset during the gap show the node was actually down; post-restart findmnt shows recovered, hardened mount state
